ABSTRACT  
The effective strategies to increase the energy density of carbon-based supercapacitors are increasing the specific 
surface area (SSA) and heteroatom doping, however the methods to achieve such outcomes are often time- 
consuming and complicated. Herein, a time-saving and facile method was adopted to fabricate hierarchical 
carbonized wood electrodes with both delignification and partly dissolution/regeneration through NaOH/thio -
urea solution followed by carbonization. The partial dissolution/regeneration treatment not only generates the 
interconnected network structures on the surface of the regenerated wood and improves the porosity, but also 
achieves the efficient co-doping of nitrogen/sulfur heteroatoms. A relatively excellent activation was achieved by 
dissolving for only 3 h, with a SSA of 1416.25 m
2
/g, which was 2.86 times higher than the SSA of the samples 
carbonized directly with delignified wood. Remarkably, the as prepared electrode exhibits superior areal (spe -
cific) capacitance of 6.11 F/cm
2 
(413.6 F/g, 1.0 mA/cm
2
) and durability (98.9%, 12,000 cycles, 50 mA/cm
2
). In 
addition, a symmetrical supercapacitor (SSC) assembled from carbonized regenerated wood has an excellent 
energy density of 1.15 mWh/cm
2 
(51.24 Wh/kg) at a power density of 699 mW/cm (31.11 W/kg). This facile 
doping and activation method may be able to provide a new concept for the carbon electrode preparation of bio- 
based materials.   
1. Introduction 
As one of the most widely used electrochemical energy storage de -
vices, supercapacitors (SCs) performing a crucial function in electro -
chemical storage and release of energy due to their potentially high 
electrochemical efficiency, long operating life, and certifiable safety ( Fu 
et al., 2021; Xu et al., 2022 ). The output performance of SCs is heavily 
relevant to the electrode substances. Carbon-based electrodes were 
regarded as promising electrode for SCs due to the presence of large 
specific surface area (SSA), adjustable pore size distribution and high 
electrical conductivity ( Wang et al., 2019b; Yang et al., 2022 ). Unfor -
tunately, the low energy density of carbon-based electrode is the major 
obstacle towards the flexible application due to the lack of structure 
optimization and control of surface properties. Therefore, finding a 
simple way to optimize the structure and control surface properties of 
carbon-based material electrodes can achieve energy density 
improvements. 
Lignocellulosic biomass-derived materials are encountering the most 
flourishing moment due to their versatile properties and wide potential 
applications( Shen and Sun, 2021 ). Controllable preparation of ligno -
cellulosic biomass-derived materials, development of new methods to 
prepare novel biomaterials from lignocellulose, and provision of envi -
ronmentally friendly, low-cost and easily scalable lignocellulosic func -
tional materials are essential to achieve carbon neutrality( Kang et al., 
2021 ). Woody biomass possesses a rich source, a wide variety, low cost, 
degradable, renewable, and a significant anisotropic and hierarchical 
structure, allowing it to be applied directly to SCs without the use of 
other conductive agents or adhesives ( Daotong et al., 2023 ). However, 
wood has a diversity of chemical components and structural complexity 
( Zhao et al., 2020 ). Due to the different distribution of the three major 
components including cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin ( Schubert 
et al., 2022 ), the uneven decomposition of the three components during

tivity and pore distribution in the thick cell walls, which results in still 
unsatisfactory electrochemical properties ( Wang et al., 2021c; Wang 
et al., 2021d; Zhang et al., 2019a ). Therefore, reducing the 
non-uniformity of conductivity and pore distribution due to the 
complexity of the wood itself is the valid methods to enhance the elec -
trode performance. In contrast to the classic bottom-up method of 
delignification in the paper and pulping industry, the top-down 
approach allows the embedded lignin to be removed from the wood 
cell wall structure while maintaining the natural anisotropic structure. 
The carbonization of wood after delignification will minimize the 
inhomogeneous pore structure produced by the complexity of the wood 
and facilitate the regulate the charge/ion transport pathway. 
The large SSA provides active sites that can retain electric charges. 
For instance, in our previous work, the delignified wood carbon elec -
trode obtained by controlling the carbonization temperature and the 
multi-stage carbonization process had a high SSA of 945.09 m

tance was 211.3 F/g (0.5 A/g), far exceeding the natural carbonized 
wood (20.6 F/g)( Luo et al., 2022a ). That is, the electrochemical per -
formance is improved by the electric double layer capacitances (EDLC) 
mechanism( He et al., 2022b ). Therefore, the activation of carbon pre -
cursors before or during the carbonization process is one of the effective 
means to increase the SSA. Wang et al. prepared carbonized wood 
through delignification followed by enzyme treatment, the pore gener -
ation was controlled by controlling the ratio and treatment time be -
tween cellulase and delignified wood. The obtained electrode had a high 
SSA (1418 m

and durability (86.58%, 15,000 cycles)( Wang 
et al., 2021c ). N, S could cause electron density imbalance and improve 
carbon surface activity due to the electronegativity difference between 
atoms( He et al., 2022a ; Wang et al., 2023 ). The surface functional 
groups could provide additional pseudo-capacitance via redox reaction, 
thus improving the weight capacitance( Lyu et al., 2023 ). Importantly, 
the introduction of heteroatoms into the carbon structure could enhance 
surface polarity and wettability could further overcome the limitations 
of carbon in structure, surface performance and electrochemical per -
formance ( Ma et al., 2020 ). However, the methods that can simulta -
neously achieve an increase in SSA and heteroatom doping were often 
complex, time-consuming and could not be obtained in one step. For 
example, Tang et al. first achieved the doping of N and S double atoms 
by soaking a mixture of delignified wood and trithiocyanuric acid so -
lution, then two high-temperature carbonizations in N
2 
and NH

, 
respectively, were performed to obtain larger SSA. The obtained wood 
carbon electrode had a high SSA (1438 m
2
/g), the specific capacitance 
(704 F/g, 0.2 A/g) and superior oxygen reduction reaction performance 
( Tang et al., 2018 ). Therefore, in order to boost the output performance 
of biomass-based carbon, we are very interested in a simple and versatile 
strategy that enables a combination of activated pore generation and 
regulation surface properties. 
Herein, an effective method was adopted to fabricate hierarchical 
carbonized wood electrodes with both delignification and partly disso -
lution/regeneration through NaOH/thiourea solution followed by 
carbonization. The delignification is to obtain a more uniform hierar -
chical structure, and the process of dissolution regeneration of the 
NaOH/thiourea reagent system is also a process of activation and het -
eroatom doping. A relatively high activation effect was achieved in three 
hours, and the SSA obtained after carbonization was 1416.25 m
2
/g, 
much higher than that of 494.89 m
2
/g for direct carbonization after 
delignification. In addition, the doping of N,S double heteroatoms in -
creases the surface wettability and improves the defects and graphiti -
zation degree of the carbon structure. Therefore, the structure of this 
regenerated wood makes it an outstanding substrate for multi- 
functionalities, which makes up for the defects of traditional 
activation and doping methods and opens new opportunities for the 
development of supercapacitors. 
2. Experiment sections 
Detailed preparation and electrochemical test methods were 
included in the Supporting Information . 
3. Result and discussion 
A schematic diagram is shown in Fig. 1 , where we describe the entire 
procedure of converting waste Larch (Natural wood, NW) to a carbon 
material through delignification, regeneration and thereafter carbon -
ization, followed by assembly into a symmetrical supercapacitor (SSC) 
device. First, delignification and bleaching methods were mentioned in 
our previous study (process I) to obtain delignified wood (TW)( Luo 
et al., 2022b ). After delignification, NaOH/thiourea solution was 
introduced to dissolve a portion of the wood cell wall. Regenerated TW-x 
(RTW-x) was obtained after regeneration and drying of the dissolved cell 
walls in ethanol, where the x represents the time of dissolution (process 
II). Specifically, NaOH can not only penetrate the microcrystals but also 
enter the microcrystals to destroy the cellulose molecules, thiourea as 
blockers can prevent the recombination of cellulose molecular chains, 
the synergistic effect enables cellulose to achieve activation and the 
introduction of N and S atoms. NaOH/thiourea solvent is an effective 
inorganic solvent for dissolving cellulose, and NaOH is considered to be 
a useful activator, so the activation and two-element doping can be 
achieved very skillfully by this method. It is worth noting that this 
method has the advantage of being rapid and safe compared to con -
ventional activation and doping methods. RTW-x was carbonized under 
inert gas (N
2
), also to gain conductive carbon wood with extensive 
surface area (Process III), and carbonized RTW-x (CRTW-x) was ob -
tained. This is expected to achieve excellent capacitive performance by 
regulating N/S content and improving porosity through partial dis -
solution/regeneration while preserving the wood microtubule structure. 
3.1. Characterization of RTW-x 
From the physical object displayed in Fig S1a and b, it can be seen 
that compared to NW, the color of TW becomes white due to the removal 
of a large amount of lignin. Particularly, given its outstanding lignin 
solubility, cellulose protection, and low energy consumption, formic 
acid has been used as a cooking agent for pulping to remove lignin from 
lignocellulosic feedstock ( Wang et al., 2019a ). In addition, the dual 
solvent system is formed by formic acid and water with the character -
istic of a high azeotropic point, which is 107. 6 º C at 101.3 kPa pressure, 
and easy recovery with distillation ( Luo et al., 2022b ). Additionally, 
deep eutectic solvent (DES) is an emerging candidate as compared to 
others due to its high efficiency, recoverability, biodegradability, and 
has a low cost of preparation ( Kesari et al., 2022 ; Sirvio et al., 2015 ). 
DES is expected to be an efficient solvent for obtaining delignified wood 
directly from wood by the "Top-down" method. After dis -
solution/regeneration, as shown in Fig. S1 c-f, it is noted that, the RTW-x 
changes into yellow. When the time was 1 – 3 h, the morphology of the 
dried RTW did not change significantly. When the dissolution time was 
longer than 3 h, however, RTW crumples after drying, which is detri -
mental to the establishment of wood-based hierarchical porous mate -
rials. Fig. 2 a. ( Fig S2a ) shows the scanning electron microscope (SEM) 
images of TW that presented a more closed block structure. Differently, 
after one hour of dissolution, RTW-1 exhibits a slight volume of pore 
structure ( Figs. 2 b and S2b ). As shown in Fig. 2 c, lots of pores and 
interwoven network appeared on the cell wall of RTW-2. RTW-3 shows 
the anisotropic multi-channel structure of the wood is preserved, and in 
the lumen with a nanofiber network is the result of regeneration 
( Fig. 2 d). The original channel structure of RTW-3 facilitates the for -
mation of interconnected layered porous structures in the subsequent

content occurred from 23.0% in NW to 1.7% in TW. However, the cel -

due to the complexity of the wood during the carbonization process. In 
this process, the density also decreased from 0.559 for NW to 0.32 g/cm
3 
for RTW-3 due to the creation of pores ( Fig. S4a ), while the porosity 
increased to 78.67% (RTW-3), which was higher than those of NW 
(62.73%) and TW (73.53%) ( Fig. S4b ). The generation of pores in the 
cell walls, the decrease in density and the increase in porosity all proved 
the superior activation effect of NaOH/thiourea, and the production of 
network structure in the lumen can effectively use the space.

crystalline structure of delignified wood, X-ray Diffraction (XRD) was 
performed ( Fig. 2 g). By analyzing the diffraction angle of NW and TW

confirmed cellulose II, which indicated that the dissolution process de -
stroys the crystalline structure ( Zhang et al., 2019b ). It is known from 
this phenomenon that the regeneration of wood from NaOH/thiourea 
solutions usually takes place in a non-ordered manner, in both amor -
phous and crystalline cellulose ( Yang et al., 2011 ). The crystallinity (CI) 
was calculated using Jade software, after delignification, the CI of TW 
was 69.80%, which was higher than that of NW at 59.26%. The CI for 
RTW-1, RTW-2 and RTW-3 were 59.00%, 41.75% and 40.08%, respec -
tively ( Fig. 2 h), which might be caused by the greater damage of cel -
lulose by NaOH/thiourea with increasing time. The FTIR spectra of the 
TW and RTW-x displayed in Fig S5 . This result indicates no change in the 
characteristic functional groups before and after regeneration, there is 
no chemical reaction did occur during the dissolution process reactions. 
The thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves of TW and RTW-x are 
presented in Fig S6 , RTW-x is less thermally stable than TW, due to the 
cellulose molecular chain were broken and less constrained, which is in 
accordance with the result of XRD. 
In natural wood, cellulose is the skeletal structure and lignin is the 
filler that provides strength to the wood. After delignification, the lignin 
is almost completely removed, which limiting the application, since its 
mechanical properties can be severely reduced. The dissolution/regen -
eration process can improve the mechanical properties of delignified 
wood, which can make it more widely available ( Tu et al., 2021 ; Ye 
et al., 2019 ). From Fig. 2 i, TW exhibited a poor tensile strength 
( σ b = 5.06 MPa) and elongation at break ( ε b = 9.14%), lower than that 
of the RTW-1 ( σ b = 11.07 MPa, ε b = 9.68%), RTW-2 ( σ b = 20.42 MPa, 
ε b = 16.22%) and RTW-3 ( σ b = 17.29 MPa, ε b = 10.34%). The 
increased mechanical strength broadens the application prospects of 
delignified wood. Regenerated wood can improve the porosity and 
mechanical strength of wood-based materials, providing a better plat -
form for the design of multifunctional materials.

In addition, we tested the electrochemical impedance (EIS) of the 
CTW and CRTW-x electrodes ( Fig. 5 g). The ohmic resistance (Rs) is 
obtained from the intercept located on the real axis. Rs was 1.733, 
1.988, 2.205 and 2.687 Ω for CRTW-3, CRTW-2, CRTW-1 and CTW, 
respectively, it represents that the carbon electrode has favorable con -
ductivity in liquid electrolyte. The diameter of the semicircle at high 
frequencies means the charge transfer resistance(Rct)( Luo et al., 2022a ). 
Clearly, the Rct of the CRTW-3 electrode ( ≈ 2.57 Ω ) is much smaller than 
that of the CTW ( ≈ 6.64 Ω ), CRTW-1 ( ≈ 4.67 Ω ) and CRTW-2 ( ≈ 2.96 Ω ), 
indicates the CRTW-3 had the lowest contact resistance. In the low 
frequency range, various slope values of electrodes of k — 2.40, 3.27, 
3.99 and 4.80 for the CTW, CRTW-1, CRTW-2 and CRTW-3 electrodes, 
respectively, while the straight lines of the CRTW-x electrodes got 
steeper with the increased dissolution time. This suggests that the pores 
created by the NaOH/thiourea solution during dissolution allow for 
more rapid charge storage in the electrode. Long useful life is one of the 
advantages of SCs. The cycling performance of all samples was evaluated 
by cycling 12,000 times at a scan rate of 50 mA/cm
2 
( Fig. 5 h). 
Compared with some conductive polymers such as polypyrrole and 
polyaniline have high electrochemical properties and are suitable can -
didates for electrodes, but they are prone to swelling and shedding 
during cycling resulting in poor cycling stability( Kumar et al., 2021 ; Zhu 
et al., 2011 ). After a long period of cycling, all samples showed a slight 
decrease in capacity, with CRTW-3 showing the least decrease of 1.1% 
and a capacitance retention rate of 98.9%, which is higher than that of 
CTW (81.5%), CRTW-1 (92.0%) and CRTW-2 (97.1%). It shows the 
cyclic stability and durability of carbon electrodes.
